On Wed, Dec 7, 2022 at 10:34 AM Leah Werchick <[contact omitted]> wrote:
ICYMI...
USAID collaborates with Meta to remove harmful content against Guatemalan judge. Last
week, LAC and the NTTF reached out to Meta to raise awareness on the Fundacion contra el
Terrorismo's (FCT) threatening posts against Guatemalan Judge Yassmin Barrios, a 2014
International Women of Courage awardee. This has been a common practice from FCT, as similar
content contributed to high-level judges and prosecutors going into exile. Meta escalated this
request and determined that, while FCT's Facebook page as a whole doesn't violate its standards,
one of the posts was confirmed as violating its "Violence & Incitement" policies and was removed.
While USAID believes FCT's behavior is recurrent and could lead to further restrictions, the
removal of this post is a step in the right direction. USAID will meet with Meta in mid-December to
create direct communications channels between Missions and Meta to flag
similar content and take down threatening posts or accounts in a speedy manner.
Leah Werchick
Senior Policy Advisor
Atrocity Prevention/Countering Violent Extremism
USAID Bureau for Conflict Prevention and Stabilization
